name: Regression Testing Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in regression testing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in regression testing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When regression testing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Check that regression testing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
3. When regression testing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
4. Keep regression testing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen regression testing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Document any non-obvious regression testing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
7. Validate regression testing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
8. Keep regression testing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
9. Re-check edge cases relevant to regression testing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
10. Prefer the simplest regression testing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
11. Measure before optimizing any regression testing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new regression testing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of regression testing correctness.
- Do not skip documenting regression testing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for regression testing, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
